title: They were enemies.
paragraphs: Violent. Cruel. Known for brutality so dark it made nations tremble.
Meanwhile, His own people—those who carried His name, heard His law, sang His psalms—were judged, scattered, broken.
Because it exposes something most people don’t want to face.
God is not impressed by proximity to truth… if your heart rejects it.
You already feel where this is going.
The Law. The prophets. The temple. The promises.
And still—one was spared, the other judged.
Because one repented… and the other pretended.
You remember the moment. The reluctant prophet walks into Nineveh, barely preaching, probably hoping they’d ignore him.
“Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!” (Jonah 3:4)
No long sermon. No emotional appeal.
The king steps down. The people fast. They cry out. Even the animals are covered in sackcloth.
They didn’t say, “We’re not that bad.”
They didn’t say, “At least we’re not like Israel.”
“Who knows? God may turn and relent and turn from His fierce anger, so that we may not perish.” (Jonah 3:9)
“When God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil way, God relented…” (Jonah 3:10)
They had prophets constantly calling them back.
“This people draw near with their mouth and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me.” (Isaiah 29:13)
Nineveh feared God without knowing Him.
Israel claimed to know God without fearing Him.
And God does not play along with religious games.
“But here’s what most people don’t realize…”
Judgment didn’t come to Israel because they sinned.
It came because they refused to repent.
Israel sinned repeatedly—and justified it spiritually.
The way truth became familiar… but not transformative.
“Because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I will spit you out of my mouth.” (Revelation 3:16)
And God is not moved by how much you know…
He is moved by whether you turn.
That’s the thread running through all of Scripture.
“Return to me, and I will return to you, says the Lord of hosts.” (Malachi 3:7)
They assumed privilege would protect them.
Because covenant without repentance becomes condemnation.
And here is where it shifts from history… to you.
There were moments you knew God was calling you to turn.
You softened the edge of it.
And that delay cost them everything.
Here’s the Gospel in the middle of this tension:
God doesn’t spare people because they deserve it.
He spares those who repent and trust in His mercy.
And that mercy is not abstract.
Because the judgment Israel deserved… and Nineveh feared…
“The Lord has laid on Him the iniquity of us all.” (Isaiah 53:6)
But as a turning toward the One who already bore the wrath.
You’re resisting the very mercy that could save you.
And the longer that goes on…
The other says, “God, have mercy on me.”
Say it plainly—“I’ve been delaying repentance.”
Or, “God, I don’t want to pretend anymore.”
Don’t keep this to yourself either.
You’ll need to come back to it when conviction fades and comfort tries to take over again.
And if you’re ready to go deeper—into real correction, real growth, real discipleship—step into it here:
Because the difference between Nineveh and Israel…
